summary: @asenfotech/unplugin-element-plus ships a postinstall backdoor that drops a detached C2 agent
details: The package's postinstall runs tooling-bootstrap.cjs, which base64-decodes an embedded payload from a split BOOTSTRAP_B64 chunk array, writes it to ~/.gradle/daemon/tooling-api-runtime.mjs under Gradle-daemon cover naming, and forks it detached via child_process.spawn with stdio 'ignore' and windowsHide. Execution is gated by sentinel paths (GameAggregator, api-gs/dictionaries.ts) to target specific victims. The dropped agent registers with https://npmjs.it.com/api/register (an npmjs.com typosquat) sending hostname, username, and OS type/release, then long-polls /api/task/<id> and dispatches operator-supplied commands: exec (arbitrary /bin/sh or cmd.exe), ls, download (fs.readFileSync of any path, POSTed to /api/file/<agent_id>/<task_id>), upload (write attacker-supplied bytes anywhere on disk), delete, ps, move, with results returned to /api/result/<id>. A C2_TLS_INSECURE environment variable disables TLS verification via NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0'. The package name mimics the legitimate unplugin-element-plus.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
